clue.text: Backward sets I had, like this?

indicators.note: backward tells us the word for sets is to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: to set something down is to put it, so sets means puts
had shortens to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Someone sheepishly admits they wrote things the wrong way round, asking if that is how it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns PUTS into STUP. The definition plays on 'Backward' a second time: a backward person is slow-witted, and 'like this?' points at that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A backward person is dim and slow, so being like that means being dull-witted.

clue.text: Wrote novel about chap, a deceptive sort

indicators.note: about means going round, so the anagram is wrapped around the name
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of the word before are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, so any chap will do

explanation.surface: A writer produces a novel about a man who turns out to be a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book the chap appears in, but it is the anagram signal; 'about' is the container signal wrapping the shuffled letters round the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is unfaithful to a partner by secretly seeing another person is a cheating, deceitful type.

clue.text: Rues the ways such a citizen negotiates

definitions.text: Rues the ways such a citizen negotiates

parts.words: Rues the ways such a citizen negotiates
parts.note: rues looks like the verb for regret, but it is the French word for streets, which a resident of the French capital walks every day

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the methods a certain townsman uses when bargaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rues' and 'negotiates' pretend to describe regret and bargaining; really a rue is a French street and to negotiate it is to find one's way along it.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of France's capital is the citizen who gets around its streets.

clue.text: Repeatedly low — as Victoria is, for example

definitions.meaning: two words that each mean low, one after the other
Victoria is a state of Australia, which lies in the far south of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'down' and 'under' mean low, hence 'Repeatedly'. Down Under is the nickname for Australia, where Victoria is a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is the colloquial name for Australia and New Zealand, the far side of the world from Britain.

clue.text: Horse, got out of bed walks unsteadily

indicators.note: walking unsteadily means staggering about, so the letters of the two words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A horse gets up from where it was lying and totters about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' rearranges BED and WALKS together into the answer; 'got out of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald-like horse with white patches on a brown or other non-black coat is described by this word.

clue.text: This business doesn't involve mass production, however

definitions.text: This business doesn't involve mass production, however

parts.words: This business doesn't involve mass production, however
parts.note: the sector of the economy that supplies help and care rather than goods, with a joke that a church service might involve mass after all

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain trade does not make goods in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'however' hints at the pun: a religious service may be a Mass, yet this business manufactures nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sector selling help such as banking or catering rather than manufactured goods is the tertiary sector.

clue.text: Appreciated greeting

definitions.meaning: a hello or reception given to a guest

explanation.definitionFit: A gift that is gladly received is wanted, and a warm reception at the door is a greeting.

clue.text: RAF manoeuvres, but not at these exercises

indicators.note: but not tells us to leave out the next word from the stunts

parts.note: the stunt flying of the Royal Air Force, loops and rolls in the air
taken as written

explanation.surface: Air force stunt flying is contrasted with some keep-fit routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes AT from AEROBATICS. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythmic workouts to raise the heart rate are a familiar kind of fitness routine.

clue.text: Liable to stall, adroitly manoeuvred

indicators.note: manoeuvred means moved around, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vehicle that tends to stall is skilfully steered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvred' rearranges ADROITLY. 'stall' looks like an engine stalling but means delaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slow and inclined to put things off is apt to stall for time.

clue.text: No buyer of book to bring author royalty?

definitions.text: No buyer of book to bring author royalty?

parts.words: No buyer of book to bring author royalty?
parts.note: someone who takes a book from a library pays nothing for it, so the writer earns no royalty from them

explanation.surface: A complaint about readers who do not buy a book and so earn its writer nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A library user takes books out on loan instead of purchasing them.

clue.text: You may be this, but not me

definitions.text: You may be this, but not me

parts.words: You may be this, but not me
parts.note: the pronoun you can refer to many people, while me only ever refers to one

explanation.surface: A teasing remark that the listener may be something the speaker is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical number for more than one; you can address several people, me never does.

clue.text: Feel nostalgic about our island state

parts.note: to feel nostalgic about something is to miss it
taken as written
I is a standard abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the home island they share with others.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Doctor drawn into Ulster conflict

indicators.note: drawn into means pulled inside, so the doctor goes within the garment

parts.note: an ulster is a long, loose overcoat
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A physician is pulled into the Northern Irish troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like Northern Ireland, but an ulster is a long Victorian overcoat; 'drawn into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting between forces is armed conflict.

clue.text: E.g. people watching TV interview

definitions.meaning: viewers are an example of a gathering of spectators
a formal meeting with an important person, as with the Pope

explanation.definitionFit: Spectators are collectively the viewers, and a formal meeting with a monarch or Pope is granted as one.

clue.text: For example, cold grouse or beef

definitions.meaning: a cold is an example of a minor illness
to grouse is to grumble, so a grouse is a grumble
a beef is a gripe or grievance

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: an ailment, and two slang words for a grumble. 'grouse' and 'beef' pretend to be food.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a minor ailment and a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Builder of small home or large cathedral

definitions.text: Builder of small home or large cathedral

parts.words: Builder of small home or large cathedral
parts.note: a tiny songbird builds a small nest, and the architect of St Paul's Cathedral in London shares its name

explanation.surface: A builder who can make anything from a cottage to a great church.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London; the little bird of the same name builds a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny brown bird nests in hedges, and Sir Christopher designed London's great cathedral.

clue.text: Take advantage of easy victory

definitions.meaning: to treat someone as a doormat is to exploit them
a win where the opponent offers no contest

explanation.definitionFit: To trample on someone is to exploit them, and a win with no real opposition is an unopposed contest.

clue.text: See a table set — what's in the middle?

indicators.note: what's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone looks at a laid table and asks what goes in the centrepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside 'See a table set', dropping the first S and last ET. The 'middle' is the belly, where food ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: Food goes into the stomach, the middle of the body, so foodstuffs are what fill it.

clue.text: Expression of surprise produced by current state

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at the present condition of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British exclamation of astonishment, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: Soldiers may be missing this idleness

definitions.meaning: soldiers listed as missing are said to be lost in battle, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it completes 'missing in action', the status of soldiers unaccounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing is the lack of activity, a state of idleness.

clue.text: Influenced by everybody, despite one's best efforts

parts.note: a work after a painter is in that painter's style, influenced by them
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Someone sways with the crowd, even though they try hard not to.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to mean in spite of everything, as in 'it failed regardless'.

clue.text: Leader of host

definitions.meaning: the lead singer who fronts a band
the presenter who fronts a television programme

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure who leads a band or presents a show is the public face of it.

clue.text: Possibly end of sail and of mast in wreckage

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way
end of means only the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Bits of sail and mast float about after a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes L from 'sail', and 'Possibly' rearranges it with OF MAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating debris from a wrecked ship is the classic term paired with jetsam.

clue.text: King's casual about source of warning

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards
lax means casual or slack
on means about, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: A monarch is relaxed about where a warning comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud electric horn, once on cars and ships, that sounds an alarm.

clue.text: Free as 5 ac, finally?

definitions.meaning: the final part of the horse word at 5 across is bald, and bald means without locks of hair

explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is SKEWBALD, which finishes in BALD; someone bald has no locks, hence 'un-locked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfastened is open or released, at liberty.

clue.text: In this case, veal is cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suitcase in which meat is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges VEAL IS; 'In this' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small suitcase or travelling bag is a type of case.

clue.text: Oriental criminals taking racket back into island

indicators.note: taking means one piece takes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese criminal gang

indicators.note: back means the word for racket is read from end to start

parts.note: din means racket or noise

explanation.surface: Asian gangsters bring a racket back onto an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives NID, and 'taking' is the container signal; 'into' is only a link. Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago.
explanation.definitionFit: The larger Caribbean island of the twin-island nation off Venezuela.

clue.text: Flower that reminds you of one or two girls

definitions.meaning: the herb is the traditional symbol of remembrance
a single girl's name, or two names, Rose and Mary, side by side

explanation.walkthrough: Ophelia in Hamlet says the herb is 'for remembrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant herb stands for memory, and the word is one girl's name or two.

clue.text: After short time, fish goes into seaweed

indicators.note: after means the fish comes after the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Following a brief spell, a fish swims into the kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of large brown kelp found on rocky coasts.
